clue.text: Girl collapsed in the race

indicators.note: a structure that has collapsed lies in a jumble, so these three words fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A runner falls over during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' sounds like a runner's mishap but tells you to rearrange the nine letters of IN THE RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female given name, so it fits the crossword's frequent use of 'girl' for a name.

clue.text: A shipping company heard to make a profit

indicators.note: heard tells you the phrase is spoken aloud and the entry is another word with that sound

parts.note: a ship's company is its crew, so this is 'a crew'

explanation.surface: A shipping firm is reported to be earning money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that accrues builds up as gain, close to earning a return.

clue.text: Trying to avoid punishment

definitions.meaning: keeping out of sight to escape someone
a beating, as in 'a good thrashing'

explanation.definitionFit: Concealing oneself is evading notice, and a thrashing is a beating: two senses of one word.

clue.text: Tell about arriving after the due time

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word meaning concerning
being behind schedule means being late

explanation.surface: Explain why you turned up behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to narrate it, a synonym of tell.

clue.text: Not taking a one-sided view

parts.note: a person who sides with neither party in a dispute; the clue is a plain description

explanation.definitionFit: Impartial, favouring no faction, is the core meaning.

clue.text: Neither here nor there

parts.note: the idiom means irrelevant, but read literally it describes some other place altogether

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, a place that is not this one nor that one is some other location.

clue.text: One church in a valley might be covered by a heavy fall of snow

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for the valley

parts.note: a vale is a poetic word for a valley
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A village chapel nestling in a mountain valley could be buried by snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AN and CH inside VALE, giving VALANCHE, with A in front. 'might be covered by' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow crashing down a mountainside is the classic sense.

clue.text: Intimidates-hits on the fore head

parts.note: the front of the head is the brow
to strike is to beat

explanation.surface: Bullying someone by striking them across the forehead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the' joins the pieces: BEATS goes with BROW, read in answer order as BROW then BEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone with stern looks and words is to cow them.

clue.text: Plant 150 too many

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
over can mean in excess, as in over the limit

explanation.surface: A gardener sets out a hundred and fifty seedlings, more than needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil-leaved forage herb, a familiar meadow species.

clue.text: Usual cod I ordered was rather sour

indicators.note: ordered suggests a restaurant meal but signals putting these letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The fish I always get at the chippy tasted a bit off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' suggests ordering food but rearranges USUAL COD I.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly acid in taste, tart or sharp.

clue.text: Colour liable to run

definitions.meaning: a hue of the spectrum, like that of a lemon

explanation.definitionFit: Both a primary hue and slang for cowardice, as in having a streak of it.

clue.text: Type of coat about to be put on new unit included, being part of it?

definitions.text: Type of coat about to be put on new unit included, being part of it?

indicators.note: put on means added after the earlier letters in this across entry

parts.note: a fur is a kind of coat

indicators.note: new tells you the following word appears in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
re is the Latin-derived word meaning concerning

explanation.surface: Upholstering a newly bought cabinet in fur, as part of the home's fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges UNIT to NITU; 'to be put on' adds RE after it. A unit (such as a kitchen cupboard) is itself one piece of the whole, which is the &lit idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Household fittings such as tables, chairs and storage units collectively.

clue.text: Opportunity of a catch not taken

definitions.meaning: an occasion when something may be done
in cricket, a dropped catch is called a missed one of these

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a fielder who drops a catch is said to have put down a chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a favourable opening and the cricket term for a catching opportunity.

clue.text: One with constructive ideas

parts.note: constructive normally means helpful, but literally it means having ideas for building

explanation.definitionFit: A designer of buildings has ideas about construction.

clue.text: Staff mind changing inside for a game!

indicators.note: inside places the rearranged letters within the word for the rod

parts.note: a staff or rod is a baton

indicators.note: changing tells you the letters of the next word alter their order

explanation.surface: Employees switch their thinking to play an indoor sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees but is a stick, BATON. 'changing' gives DMIN from MIND, and 'inside' puts it within BATON.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: If patient, one might get to ride in it

definitions.text: If patient, one might get to ride in it

parts.words: If patient, one might get to ride in it
parts.note: patient seems to mean willing to wait, but here a sick person is carried to hospital

explanation.definitionFit: An emergency vehicle that carries the sick or injured to hospital.

clue.text: Secretive number in Surrey disheartened

indicators.note: in places the numeral within the remaining letters
losing its heart means the county name keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A hush-hush figure in the Home Counties feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: SURREY, an English county south of London, keeps only its first and last letters, S and Y, around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty and furtive, acting in a covert way.

clue.text: Resort not in the country

indicators.note: not tells you a word is left out of the country's name

parts.note: a country, here the Iberian nation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday destination not to be found in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' suggests rural areas but is a nation, SPAIN; 'not in' removes IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A town with healing mineral springs where people go to relax.

clue.text: Nevertheless I leave the abominable creature

indicators.note: leave means the letter departs from the creature's name

parts.note: the Abominable Snowman of the Himalayas

explanation.surface: Still, I'll keep away from the monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym for however or even so.

clue.text: Sort of plan to help one on the way

definitions.text: Sort of plan to help one on the way

parts.words: Sort of plan to help one on the way
parts.note: a strategy for reaching a goal, and literally a chart for travelling

explanation.definitionFit: A strategic plan, and literally a chart of streets for travellers.

clue.text: You will not hear a sound out of it

definitions.text: You will not hear a sound out of it

parts.words: You will not hear a sound out of it
parts.note: sounds sound like silence, but means beyond the range of hearing

explanation.definitionFit: Out of range of hearing, a sound cannot be heard.

clue.text: Scenes MPs make

definitions.meaning: a division of a play containing scenes

explanation.walkthrough: MPs are Members of Parliament, who pass laws known as Acts of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a section of a play made of scenes and a statute that Parliament passes.

clue.text: Blackbird?

parts.note: the question mark hints at a small bird whose name starts with a black fuel

explanation.walkthrough: Not the thrush called a blackbird: a small British songbird whose name begins with a black fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A small titmouse, named after coal for its black head.

clue.text: Deceive with a lump of toffee

definitions.meaning: a striped boiled mint sweet, popular in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: A verb for hoodwinking and the name of a hard British peppermint sweet.

clue.text: Councillor puts a tax on an item of clothing

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a sales tax

explanation.surface: A local politician imposes a levy on garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckerchief worn tucked into the collar, a garment.

clue.text: Pat and Len going round earth perhaps

indicators.note: going round suggests circling, but here it tells you to turn these letters about

explanation.surface: Two friends travel all over the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' rearranges PAT and LEN; 'perhaps' shows earth is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Our world is one example of a body orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Sort of orange wild in Asia

indicators.note: sort here is a verb meaning arrange, so the next word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of citrus that grows wild in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Asian wild ass; 'Sort of' rearranges ORANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild ass native to the deserts of Asia.

clue.text: Afraid Lyn could have come from an imaginary country

indicators.note: the answer could be produced from these letters by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A frightened girl may have arrived from a land of make-believe.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic realm of elves and sprites, a make-believe land.

clue.text: One or two similar containers?

parts.note: a single metal food vessel, and also two words each naming a vessel

explanation.definitionFit: A metal food canister, whose two halves each name a container.

clue.text: Boy to get on in Hertfordshire

parts.note: Steven is a boy's name
to get on in years is to grow old, to age

explanation.surface: A young man hopes to succeed in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: HERTFORDSHIRE is a county just north of London; the answer is a new town there. 'get on' seems to mean prosper but means grow older.
explanation.definitionFit: A town located in that county, the first of Britain's post-war new towns.

clue.text: Fawn right in the grass

indicators.note: in places the letter for right inside the grass

parts.note: couch grass is a common weed grass

explanation.surface: A young deer lies hidden right in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawn' looks like a deer but is the verb, to cringe or grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower and cringe low before someone, the servile sense of fawn.

clue.text: Coach to remain outside according to the law

indicators.note: outside places the word for stay around the other piece

parts.note: to stay is to remain
a private tutor coaches students

explanation.surface: A trainer must wait outside, as the rules require.
explanation.definitionFit: Required or permitted by statute, legally prescribed.
